reason: Git operates on a working tree you have to be able to move around in first.
You can write markup in any editor; every tool that serves it lives behind a prompt.
The array work is taught against a rendered document, so the document has to exist first.
You cannot annotate a signature until you can read what a function does to its arguments.
Component state is declared through typed props and hooks; untyped state hides its own bugs.
Every state update is an array or object transform; mutation in place breaks rendering.
Server rendering is a decision about where state resolves, so you need state first.
Schema work runs fine in a GUI client; the shell is how you load and dump it fast.
An index is a promise about a schema. No schema, nothing to index.
A contract can be written before the schema, but it will leak whatever the schema got wrong.
Types make a contract executable; you can still specify one in prose.
Interpreters, virtual environments and test runners are all invoked from the shell.
Validation is a function over input. Write the function first.
An endpoint's request and response models are the validation layer, exposed.
Versioning discipline shapes the route surface, but a first endpoint ships without it.
You containerize a service. There has to be a service.
Builds, tags and runs are shell operations, and the failures are read in logs.
Structured output is a schema you hand the model; unvalidated output is just a string.
A tool call is a model call with a contract at both ends.
Serving experience makes the transport obvious; MCP can be learned from the spec alone.
Chunking is text processing: pure functions over strings, tested.
You embed chunks, and the chunk boundary decides what a vector can mean.
Vector retrieval is an indexed query; without index literacy top-k is a mystery.
Retrieval has nothing to search without stored vectors.
The pipeline ends in a generation call that has to hold a schema.
You can build it unmeasured, you just won't know if it works.
A budget is only meaningful once you are the one filling the window.
Knowing what you spent context on tells you what to measure; the ladder can be built either way.
You cannot score outputs you cannot reliably produce.
Observability is configured at the image and platform boundary.
The thing being observed in the capstone is the pipeline.
A deployed interface is the usual first consumer of your traces; a service alone will do.
